newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Commission not liable for Guerin Autos insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Court says Commission not liable for Guerin Autos insolvency.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Thursday a plea from Guerin Autos to find the European Commission pushed it into bankruptcy when it failed to act against Nissan France's exclusive distributorship system.
In dismissing the application as inadmissible, the court found no causal link between the Commission's alleged failure to act and Guerin's forced liquidation.

"Even if it can be established that the Commission was guilty of failure to act...the applicant has failed to provide any indication in its application capable of explaining to what extent the Commission was liable for the damage," the court said.

Because the Commission had been late to notify Guerin of its position on the complaint against Nissan, the court said the Commission was largely responsible for the legal action taken by Guerin and ordered the Commission to pay its own costs and half of the applicant's cost.

application for (i) a declaration that the Commission failed to act, by not addressing a statement of objections to Nissan France and (ii) compensation for the damage caused to the applicant by that failure to act
1. Declares that there is no need to rule on the action for failure to act;
2. Dismisses the remainder of the application as inadmissible;
3. Orders the Commission to pay its own costs and half of the applicant's costs.
